outcome: levels of antispike, receptor binding domain and nucleocapsid antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 in mothers
neutralizing antibodies from mother-infant dyads in maternal and umbilical cord blood at birth
cohort: A cohort of 178 pregnant women who received COVID-19 vaccination.
finding: COVID-19 vaccination significantly increased maternal antispike and receptor binding domain immunoglobulin G levels, and vaccination in the early second trimester provided the optimum balance between maternal antibody response and placental antibody transfer to the neonate.
followup_time: At birth (for mother-infant dyads), and 15 days after the first and second vaccination (for maternal antibodies)
